assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues is a genuine molecular design principle: a small molecule is engineered to recruit an E3 ligase to a target and thereby change what chemists and clinicians can do, including against proteins once called undruggable. Impact spans chemical biology, medicinal chemistry and now clinical oncology and immunology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glue degraders and underpins the clinical IMiD story. Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray have strong contributions but a three-person split of concept, E3-ligase mechanism and glue biology seems defensible. Credit for the first PROTAC versus later optimization is still a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Many clinical-stage degraders and approved IMiD-class drugs, with independent replication across hundreds of laboratories. Clinical validation of heterobifunctional PROTACs is still maturing, but the underlying chemistry is firmly established, so recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Whether a heterobifunctional PROTAC has yet reached approval, which I cannot verify.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others is contested; Handa's part is mechanistic rather than a design invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, a case where molecular lipid design (pKa tuning, self-assembly, endosomal escape) directly changed medicine for hundreds of millions of people. This is the kind of chemistry-to-clinic path I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established ionizable-lipid LNP formulation and scalable assembly; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidomimetic and polymer nanocarrier discovery. Hope, Madden and MacLachlan were also decisive and the group of six may force hard choices, and the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification already recognized the mRNA side.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed by approved products (patisiran, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines) and many independent lipid generations. Mature and timely, though the Medicine prize overlap may reduce room.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize may make the committee reluctant.
Patent and priority disputes among LNP developers complicate credit; I cannot verify the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are chemistry-driven genome editors: deaminase chemistry is fused to a programmable nickase to rewrite single bases without double-strand breaks. Strong precision, broad adoption in biomedicine, and a first clinical translation make this a clear, original invention.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the concept and development, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, requiring directed evolution of a new deaminase) as lead inventors. Nishida and Kondo reported a parallel cytidine deaminase approach, which complicates exclusive credit. Liu also appears in prime editing, which should probably be folded into one recognition.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, with clinical trials under way and early patient benefit reported. CRISPR was recognized in 2020, so base editing is a natural, mature follow-on.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to honor Liu for base and prime editing together rather than separately.
Strength of the Nishida and Kondo claim to co-credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing replaced Sanger sequencing and transformed biology and medicine. The chemistry (reversible terminator nucleotides, clonal clusters on surfaces, sequencing-by-synthesis) is original, and sequencing is the default readout across diagnostics, microbiology and genomics.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry; Rothberg's pyrosequencing-on-chip approach gave the 454 platform. Mayer and Ju are also credited and several platforms (Illumina, 454, nanopore) complicate any claim of a single decisive invention.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature and field-defining over two decades, so if anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Chemistry versus technology and instrument engineering: the committee may see this as closer to Medicine or Physics in character.
Priority conflicts between Solexa and other early sequencing-by-synthesis efforts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing turns single-molecule translocation into an electrical readout and has become a commercial DNA and RNA sequencer, while engineered protein pores from the Bayley lab opened a general platform for stochastic sensing. As a biosensor person I value the molecular-design aspect, with a path from concept to portable devices.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer and colleagues provided the founding concept and proof of principle; Bayley engineered the alpha-hemolysin pore; Akeson demonstrated reading DNA with a polymerase motor. Priority is spread widely, and a trio of Bayley, Branton and Deamer is plausible but excludes decisive later work.
assessment.maturity: Commercial nanopore sequencing is widely deployed and independently validated; the field still evolves, with protein sequencing and solid-state pores being worked on.
uncertainties: The decisive contribution among five or more credited people is genuinely unclear, and whether all proposed laureates are alive is something I cannot verify.
Engineering of Oxford Nanopore devices is partly commercial work outside this credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists install designed noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, a general tool for protein chemistry, biophysics and biotherapeutics. Directly relevant to molecular design with precise control.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach and its first demonstrations; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to synthetic genomes and orthogonal ribosomes; Lei Wang contributed early mammalian and neuronal applications. Mehl and Yokoyama also made important advances.
assessment.maturity: Validated for twenty years in many laboratories with applications in antibody-drug conjugates and photocrosslinking, though routine clinical use remains limited.
uncertainties: Impact is broad in research but less transformative for patients than some other candidates.
Division of credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C cysteine turned a protein considered undruggable into a drug target, and his analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics gave a general tool for dissecting signaling. This is a clean chemical idea with direct clinical consequence (sotorasib, adagrasib).
assessment.attribution: Credit is concentrated in a single credited person, which makes a prize configuration simple, though KRAS drug development involved many companies and groups and the clinical drugs were built on later optimization.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs and strong reproducibility, but the clinical story is only a few years old and resistance is a concern. Reasonably timely rather than overdue.
uncertainties: Some may prefer to pair Shokat with other contributors to kinase or KRAS chemistry, who are not listed here.
Durability of clinical benefit given resistance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly provides programmable, sequence-encoded control over nanomaterial organization, and spherical nucleic acids have created a distinct class of biosensing and gene-regulation agents. This sits right in my area, though I judge impact on broad practice to be smaller than for the higher-ranked entries.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's lab developed the gold-nanoparticle DNA conjugates and spherical nucleic acid concept; Alivisatos independently reported DNA-directed nanocrystal assembly at the same time. Mucic and Storhoff were early trainees, so a one- or two-person configuration seems fair.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent follow-up in diagnostics and nanomaterials, with clinical translation of spherical nucleic acids still modest.
uncertainties: Translational impact of spherical nucleic acids has not yet matched expectations.
Priority between Mirkin and Alivisatos groups, and relative importance of Alivisatos's wider nanocrystal work.
